newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRODEUR BOUNCES BACK FROM BENCHING TO SHUT OUT PANTHERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRODEUR BOUNCES BACK FROM BENCHING TO SHUT OUT PANTHERS.

text.p: Martin Brodeur, bouncing back from a benching, posted his second shutout of the season and added an assist Tuesday as the New Jersey Devils blanked the league-best Florida Panthers 2-0.
Brodeur, who whitewashed Detroit a month ago, made 28 saves to end a personal three-game losing streak.
"I felt pretty good. I've been working real hard yesterday and this morning and felt really comfortable coming in," said Brodeur, benched in favour of Dunham on Saturday at Colorado.
"(I was) a little nervous, but I made that big stop right at the start, so that helped. Sometimes that happens and that's where the goalie has to come up big."

Brodeur set the tone early when he made a sliding stop on Scott Mellanby off a goalmouth scramble 20 seconds into the first period. He also denied Jody Hull twice in the final six minutes of the third.
Brian Rolston and Dave Andreychuk scored as the Devils won for just the second time in six games. Andreychuk's goal found the empty net at the end after Brodeur cleared away a shot.
The Devils returned home after a 1-3 road trip and broke a five-game losing streak against the Panthers.

John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 32 shots for Florida, which had its six-game unbeaten streak snapped. The Panthers lost for only the second time on the road this season but still own the best road record in the league (8-2-3).
"I had no worries (about Brodeur)," said New Jersey coach Jacques Lemaire. "Martin always bounces back, even when he struggles at times. It's the sign of a great goaltender."
In Detroit, Brendan Shanahan scored a power-play goal with 2:28 left in the third period as the Detroit Red Wings rallied for a 2-2 tie against the outgunned Vancouver Canucks.
Shanahan took a slap shot that bounced off defenceman Jyrki Lumme's right skate and past goaltender Corey Hirsch, who made 39 saves.

Detroit, which had the only shot in overtime, is 4-2-2 in its last eight games. The Red Wings, who outshot the Canucks 41-15, had a chance to win but Sergei Fedorov's slap shot hit the bottom left post with 15 seconds remaining.
"It's a terrific road point for effort, if not anything else," said Tom Renney, coach of Vancouver (13-11-1). "It wasn't pretty, but we got the job done."

At New York, Travis Green scored two goals and set up the other and linemate Zigmund Palffy added a goal and an assist, leading the New York Islanders to their third win in four games, a 3-1 triumph over the punchless Calgary Flames.
Eric Fichaud made 25 saves and earned his first win in a month for the Islanders, who moved within two points of the idle New York Rangers for fifth in the Atlantic Division.

Green's goal with 3:35 left in the first period lifted New York into a 1-1 tie and he scored again at 1:41 of the second to put the Islanders ahead to stay. Green picked up an assist on Palffy's insurance goal with nine minutes left in the game.

In Pittsburgh, Geoff Sanderson's power-play tally midway through the third period capped a two-goal comeback and Jason Muzzatti stopped five shots in overtime as the Hartford Whalers earned a 4-4 tie with the Pittsburgh Penguins.

Sanderson tied it with 8:17 left. Former Penguin Paul Coffey took a shot from the left point and goaltender Ken Wregget made the stop. But the puck trickled down his body and a streaking Sanderson pushed it between his pads to knot it.

The Penguins dominated overtime, nearly scoring when Mario Lemieux gathered the puck behind the net with just over two minutes left and fed a cross-crease pass to Jaromir Jagr, who was unable to get his stick on the puck.
Jagr scored in the second period for his eighth goal in a five-game goal-scoring streak. He leads the league with 23.
In Toronto, rookie Marcel Cousineau made 18 saves before leaving with an injury and Felix Potvin stopped 10 shots, leading the Maple Leafs to a 2-0 win over the St Louis Blues.

Cousineau had to leave after taking an elbow in the face from Blues winger Stephane Matteau with 5:57 left in the second period. Cousineau's mask was knocked off and he fell back onto the ice. He was diagnosed with a slight concussion.
Wendel Clark scored a power-play goal and Mats Sundin added a shorthanded tally in the first period for the Leafs.
In Phoenix, Ray Ferraro had a goal and an assist in a three-goal first period and Byron Dafoe made 35 saves to lead the Los Angeles Kings to a 4-1 win over the Phoenix Coyotes.

Newly acquired Brad Smyth, Rob Blake and Vladimir Tsyplakov also scored and Kevin Stevens had two assists for the Kings, who won for the second time in seven games. Los Angeles had scored just nine goals in its previous six games.
"The big difference tonight was that we didn't take a lot of foolish penalties," Kings coach Larry Robinson said. "We have been and they've killed our momentum."
